title: graduated-evacuation-profiles-with-cost-weighted-signalization
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Current canary aborts are binary and insensitive to heterogeneous signal priorities (latency vs error vs token cost) and to per-cohort throughput variance. This leads to either noisy aborts during traffic spikes or slow responses to real regressions tied to token cost increases. Goal: Deliver a graduated evacuation controller that composes multiple SLO signals into a cost-weighted score and drives staged traffic reduction instead of immediate 100% rollbacks. The controller should support: 1) per-cohort weighting (e.g., mobile vs web, premium vs free) 2) token-cost normalization (per-request expected token budget) 3) percentile-based windows (p99, p95) and rate-aware thresholding 4) hysteresis and decay to avoid oscillation, and 5) a policy DSL to express staged evacuation steps (e.g., 90% -> 50% -> 10% over configurable intervals) Approach: - Define a normalized scoring function: score = w_latency * latency_norm + w_error * error_rate_norm + w_cost * token_cost_norm - where each norm is computed against a rolling baseline (14-day median + MAD) and capped to [0,1]. - Convert score into a staged traffic policy using bucketing thresholds and a ramp plan. For example: score < 0.25 = keep; 0.25–0.5 = reduce to 90%; 0.5–0.75 = reduce to 50%; >0.75 = reduce to 10% then pause rollouts. - Introduce throughput-adjusted windows: for low-throughput cohorts compute confidence using Poisson/Binomial smoothing; for high-throughput cohorts use direct percentiles. - Tie synthetic probes: synthetic checks can force a floor on confidence and accelerate staging if they fail. - Expose policy as part of rollout config in the Console and API: rollout.policy = { signal_weights, thresholds, stage_windows, decay_seconds, min_cohort_qps } - Provide a simulator and backtest tool (local) to run past traffic and produce expected evacuation curves. Trade-offs considered: - Aggressive staging reduces blast radius but increases time-to-detect regressions; we mitigate by allowing emergency immediate-evacuate flag and synthetic-probe overrides. - Token-cost signal is noisy for short runs; we use per-request expected token budget to normalize and only use cost signal when cohort sample size > min_qps. - Complexity vs UX: offer simple presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) while allowing advanced DSL for platform teams. Observability & alerts: - New dashboard: "Evacuation Scorecard" per-rollout with stacked signal contributions, current stage, and projected traffic curve. - Alerts: score-crossing alert (with rate-limited noise suppression), and stage-change audit events. API/Console changes: - Rollout policy JSON schema additions and validation. - New UI controls for presets and manual stage override. Backwards compatibility: - Default behavior for rollouts without a policy remains immediate abort on legacy thresholds. Migration plan: stage opt-in for dedicated customers first, then opt-out for hosted after 2-week pilot. Metrics to track in pilot: false-positive aborts, time-to-evacuation, customer error uplift, token-cost delta, and rollback reversions. Acceptance criteria: 1) End-to-end policy can be attached to canary rollouts and enact staged traffic changes in a test cluster. 2) Score computation matches simulator outputs within 5% on historical test data. 3) Console shows evacuation scorecard and stage history for pilot rollouts. 4) No increase in mean time-to-recover for rollouts in pilot compared to baseline. 5) Security review completed for rollout API changes.
acceptance_criteria: Policy applies to a canary rollout and reduces traffic in configured stages
Score computation validated against simulator with <5% error on historical traces
Evacuation Scorecard visible in Console with per-signal contribution bars
Audit events emitted for each stage transition and manual overrides
Pilot rollout shows no increase in mean time-to-recover vs baseline
comments: 2025-02-11: Kickoff sync with PM and Design (notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/rollout-evacuation). Agreed to three presets and an advanced DSL. Action: engineering to prototype scoring function.

2025-02-17: Prototype scoring module implemented (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evac-controller/pull/58). Initial unit tests for normalization baselines added. Observed skew in token_cost_norm for short sessions — added min_qps gating.
2025-02-22: Design review completed. Console mockups updated (Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/evacuation-scorecard). PM requested a compact view for mobile dashboards.

2025-02-25: Ran backtest on last 30 days of rollouts in staging and compared against legacy aborts. Results: reduced full-evacuations by 42% while catching 95% of high-error events within two stages. Simulator adjustments: increase decay_seconds from 600 to 1200 for high-variance cohorts.

2025-02-28: Security review kickoff. Token-cost normalization approach reviewed for data leakage risk — approved; ensure KMS usage for any raw traffic artifacts. Open action: add redaction for prompt text in exported traces (ticketed separately).

2025-03-02: Integration tests passing in staging. Next: enable pilot for two internal product cohorts and monitor for 2 weeks. Created pilot dashboard (internal link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/evac/pilot)
